h1:
Where to Stay in Hua Hin?
12 Hotels We Actually Reviewed
Prices Compared Across 3 Sites!
heroSub: 12 hand-picked Hua Hin hotels across every budget — from 5-star beachfront resorts down to a central hostel from ฿390/night. Covering the three main areas: central Hua Hin beach, Khao Takiap, and Khao Tao / Sai Noi beach. From roughly ฿390–13,000/night.
introH2: 🏖️ Why does choosing the right area in Hua Hin matter so much?
introHtml: Hua Hin stretches for kilometres along the coast, and each area has a distinctly different feel. Central Hua Hin beach is the hub — beach, malls, the night market, the train station and accommodation at every price point, the easiest base to get around. Khao Takiap sits at the southern end of the beach with a wider, quieter stretch of sand — the beachfront resort zone, near Cicada Market. Khao Tao / Sai Noi beach is a tiny fishing village about 12 km south of town, with a quiet, private beach. Many people book without checking the area, then lose hours driving back and forth. This guide rounds up 12 Hua Hin hotels we've already reviewed across every tier — with real guest-review scores, a 3-site price comparison and direct booking links for each.
mrtHtml: Hua Hin has no metro. Getting around means your own car, rental car, scooter, taxi, or a songthaew within central Hua Hin. From Bangkok it's about 2.5–3 hours by car, or you can take the train or a minivan. In town you can walk to the beach and the night market easily, but if you're staying at Khao Takiap or Khao Tao a car is more convenient. The areas in this guide: Central Hua Hin beach — beach, malls, night market, train station, walk everywhere · Khao Takiap — wider, quieter beach at the southern end, ~10 min from town, near Cicada Market · Khao Tao / Sai Noi beach — quiet beach, fishing village, ~12 km from town.

entries.name: Centara Grand Beach Resort & Villas Hua Hin
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Central Hua Hin beach · beachfront, walk to night market

rooms.type: Deluxe Room · garden / partial sea view
Premium Deluxe Club · Club Lounge access

tags: 🏖️ On the beach in central Hua Hin
entries.addr: 1 Damnernkasem Road, Hua Hin, Prachuap Khiri Khan
entries.storyHtml: Centara Grand is a heritage resort built around the former Railway Hotel of 1923, right on the beach in central Hua Hin, scoring 9.3 from 243 reviews. Its charm is the old colonial architecture set in wide seafront gardens, with everything from heritage-wing rooms to private pool villas. Real guest reviews praise the location — you can walk to the beach and the night market — and the gardens and pools. Worth knowing: it's a grand old resort, so some rooms in the older wing feel more classic than modern; choose your room type by the style you prefer.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a seafront feel, look at rooms in the beach-side zone; for the heritage character, pick the older wing. An evening stroll through the seafront gardens is the highlight here.
pros: The 1923 Railway Hotel building — genuine heritage and history
On the beach in central Hua Hin, walk to the night market
Wide seafront gardens and lovely pools, restful setting
Multiple zones, from heritage rooms to private pool villas
cons: A grand old resort — some older-wing rooms feel classic, not new
High-season and long-weekend prices climb steeply

entries.name: Hyatt Regency Hua Hin
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Khao Takiap beachfront · southern end of the beach
entries.addr: 91 Hua Hin - Khao Takiap Road, Nong Kae, Hua Hin
entries.storyHtml: Hyatt Regency is a 5-star beachfront resort at Khao Takiap, and the most-reviewed of the luxury picks with 314 reviews, scoring 9.3. Its heart is The Barai, a water-temple-style spa that many guests book here specifically to try. The resort spreads low through wide tropical gardens with a private beach. Real guest reviews praise the space, the leafy gardens, the varied breakfast and staff who remember your name. Worth knowing: Khao Takiap means a 10–15 minute drive into town, and a long-running resort means some rooms show their age.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're coming for The Barai, look at packages that include the spa rather than paying separately, and book treatments ahead as they fill fast. Travelling with kids, ask for a Pool Access room — you step straight into the pool from the balcony.
pros: Most-reviewed luxury pick at 314 reviews · 9.3 score
Private beach plus pools in wide tropical gardens
The Barai spa is beautiful and well run — the signature here
Varied breakfast; friendly staff who remember guests
cons: Khao Takiap means a 10–15 min drive into central Hua Hin
A long-running resort — some rooms show their age

entries.name: Putahracsa Hua Hin
entries.mrtTag: 📍 South Hua Hin · Naebkehardt area · walk to night market

rooms.type: La Canna Beachfront Pool Villa (140 sqm)

tags: 🚶 Walk along the beach into town
entries.addr: 22/65 Naebkehardt Road, Hua Hin, Prachuap Khiri Khan
entries.storyHtml: Putahracsa is a 5-star boutique beachfront resort in the Naebkehardt area, the most-reviewed of the boutique picks with 343 reviews, scoring 9.2. It's beachfront yet still central, so you can walk along the sand into town. Rooms range from contemporary Urban Rooms in the main building to beachfront pool villas, suiting both couples and families. Real guest reviews praise the beachfront setting, the design and the easygoing service — a good fit for anyone who wants a beachfront boutique at a gentler price than the big chains.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For honeymooners or anyone wanting a private pool, look at the Oceanbed or La Canna beachfront villas. Urban Rooms in the main building don't have direct sea views, so pick your room type before booking.
pros: Most-reviewed boutique at 343 · steady 9.2 score
Beachfront in Naebkehardt, walk along the sand into town
Beachfront pool villas — great for couples and honeymooners
Contemporary design, easygoing service, under chain prices
cons: Urban Rooms in the main building lack direct sea views — choose carefully
Small resort — beachfront rooms sell out fast in high season

entries.name: InterContinental Hua Hin Resort
entries.badge: 🛍️ Beachfront in town, walk to the mall
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Central Hua Hin beach · next to BluPort mall
tags: 🏖️ Beachfront in the heart of town
entries.storyHtml: InterContinental Hua Hin is an IHG 5-star resort on the beach in the heart of town, right by BluPort mall, scoring 9.2 from 176 reviews. It's a location few luxury resorts in Hua Hin can match — want the sea, walk to the beach; want food and shopping, the mall is right there. The design is modern, with pools and wide gardens, and there are pet-friendly rooms. Real guest reviews praise the location, breakfast and warm service. Worth knowing: soundproofing between some rooms isn't great.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Soundproofing is a point reviews flag — ask for a high floor or the Beach Wing and note it on booking. For a direct sea view, choose an Ocean View room rather than the standard.
pros: Beachfront in the heart of town, right by BluPort mall
Modern design with pools and wide gardens
Pet-friendly rooms — uncommon at a luxury resort
Varied breakfast; warm service
cons: Soundproofing between some rooms and corridors isn't great
High-season prices are steep; standard rooms lack direct sea views

entries.name: Mövenpick Asara Resort & Spa Hua Hin
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Khao Takiap / north Hua Hin · near the beach
tags: 💬 368 reviews — the most in the guide
entries.storyHtml: Mövenpick Asara is an all-suite and pool villa resort (Mövenpick/Accor) with the most reviews in this guide — 368, scoring 9.0. Every room is a suite starting around 120 sqm, very spacious, and there are private pool villas for families and groups. The resort is laid out around a lagoon and gardens for a private feel. Real guest reviews praise the spacious, good-value suites, the lagoon and pools, and the service. Worth knowing: it's not directly on the beach but close to it, a short walk or drive away.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Travelling as a group or family, the 1–2 bedroom pool villas are great value for the private pool. Even the Junior Suite is far larger than a standard resort room — pick by budget.
pros: Most-reviewed in the guide at 368 · every room is a suite
Suites start around 120 sqm — spacious and good value
Private pool villas, great for families and groups
Lagoon and wide gardens, a private feel
cons: Not directly beachfront — a short walk or drive to the sand
Large resort, fairly long walks within the grounds

entries.name: Anantasila Beach Resort Hua Hin
entries.badge: 🌟 Top score in the guide · beachfront value
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Khao Takiap beach · Nong Kae · beachfront
entries.addr: 33/17 Soi Hua Don 7, Nong Kae, Hua Hin, Prachuap Khiri Khan
entries.storyHtml: Anantasila is a 4-star beachfront resort on Khao Takiap beach, and the highest-scoring hotel in this guide at 9.6 from 80 reviews. It's a small resort right on the sand — wake up and walk straight onto the beach — from just ฿2,800, which makes it stand out for value among beachfront rooms. There are spacious suites and pet-friendly rooms for guests bringing a dog. Real guest reviews praise the beachfront setting, the quiet and the attentive service. Worth knowing: Khao Takiap is about 10 minutes by car from the main town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Reviews single out the beachfront and the quiet — couples or small families can step up to the Junior Suite for more space at a small premium, and pets are welcome in the pet-friendly rooms.
pros: Top score in the guide at 9.6 — beachfront at a low price
On Khao Takiap beach, step straight onto the sand
Spacious suites, from just ฿2,800
Pet-friendly rooms for guests bringing a dog
cons: Khao Takiap is ~10 min by car from the main town
Small resort — beachfront rooms fill fast on long weekends

entries.name: Asira Boutique HuaHin
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Central Hua Hin · near markets and train station

rooms.type: Sala Deluxe Room · many open onto the pool

tags: 💦 Many rooms open onto the saltwater pool
entries.addr: 4 Damrongrat Road (Soi Hua Hin 51), Hua Hin, Prachuap Khiri Khan
entries.storyHtml: Asira is a 4-star design boutique in central Hua Hin where many rooms open straight onto the saltwater pool, scoring 9.3 from 163 reviews. Its in-town location means you can walk to the markets and it's near the train station — handy for eating, shopping and sightseeing. The design leans on calm and greenery, a fit for couples and anyone who wants a quiet stay in town. Real guest reviews praise the design, the pool and the warm service. Worth knowing: it's not on the beach, so it's a short drive to the sand.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a resort-in-the-city feel, ask for a Sala Deluxe that opens onto the pool. Travelling as three, the Deluxe Triple fits comfortably so you don't need two rooms.
pros: Attractive boutique design, many rooms open onto the saltwater pool
In-town location, walk to markets, near the train station
Quiet setting — good for couples and a restful stay in town
Warm service, high 9.3 review score
cons: Not on the beach — a short drive to the sand
Small property — pool-access rooms fill fast

entries.name: G Hua Hin Resort & Mall
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Central · near train station, walk to Market Village
tags: 🏊 Pool Access rooms step into the pool
entries.addr: 250/201 Soi Phetchkasem 94, Hua Hin, Prachuap Khiri Khan
entries.storyHtml: G Hua Hin is a 4-star city resort in the centre of town with its own mall and a spot near the train station, scoring 9.4 from 126 reviews. Its strength is convenience all in one place — shops downstairs, near Market Village, and easy onward travel. There are Pool Access rooms you step into the pool from, and several family room types, from just ฿1,600, which is good value for a central 4-star. Real guest reviews praise the convenience, the clean rooms and how well it suits families.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Travelling with family, look at the Family Room or Family Suite with extra sofa beds. To swim easily, choose a Deluxe Pool Access and step straight into the pool from your room.
pros: Has its own mall, all-in-one convenience, near Market Village
From just ฿1,600 — good value for a central 4-star
Pool Access rooms and several family room types
Near the train station, easy onward travel
cons: Not on the beach — a drive to the sand
A city resort — built for convenience more than sea views

entries.name: Maven Stylish Hotel Hua Hin
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Central · 5-min walk to the beach, near train station

rooms.type: Corner Suite with Balcony · corner room

entries.addr: 120/99 Phetkasem Road, Hua Hin, Prachuap Khiri Khan
entries.storyHtml: Maven is a 4-star design hotel in central Hua Hin, about a 5-minute walk to the beach, scoring 9.4 from 84 reviews. It's a stylish, contemporary stay from just ฿1,800, with a central location that walks to the beach, the markets and the train station. There's a pool and Pool View rooms to choose from. Real guest reviews praise the design, the cleanliness, the walk-everywhere location and the value — a good fit for couples and solo travellers who want a smart hotel in town without the high price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a pool view, the Superior Pool View costs only a little more. Travelling as a couple wanting more lounging space, the Corner Suite has a larger balcony.
pros: Stylish contemporary design, from just ฿1,800
Central location, 5-min walk to the beach, near the train station
Has a pool and Pool View rooms
Clean rooms, good value — great for couples and solo travellers
cons: A small hotel with relatively few reviews (84)
Not directly on the beach, though it's a 5-minute walk

entries.name: Litera Hostel Hua Hin
entries.mrtTag: 📍 In town · Soi Hua Hin 67 · 2-min walk to the beach

rooms.type: Bed in 8-bed mixed dorm · curtains, plug, reading light

entries.addr: 113/21 Soi Hua Hin 67, Hua Hin, Prachuap Khiri Khan
entries.storyHtml: Litera Hostel is the cheapest stay in this guide — from just ฿390, yet scoring a high 9.4 from 222 reviews. It's an adults-only hostel in central Hua Hin, about a 2-minute walk to the beach, near the night market and the train station. Dorms come in 4/6/8-bed configurations, every bed with privacy curtains, a plug and a reading light. Real guest reviews praise the cleanliness, the good design, the central location and the great value. A great fit for backpackers and budget travellers who want to be based in town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For more privacy and the quietest sleep, choose the 4-bed dorm with fewer people. It's adults-only (18+), so families with children need a different option.
pros: Cheapest in the guide, from ฿390 · high 9.4 score
Central, 2-min walk to the beach, near the night market
Every bed has privacy curtains, a plug and a reading light
Clean, well-designed, excellent value for backpackers
cons: Shared dorms, adults-only 18+ — not for families with kids
No hotel-level amenities

tags: 🌊 Quiet Sai Noi beach, Khao Tao

entries.storyHtml: Sanae Beach is a small beachfront boutique resort of just 12 rooms on Sai Noi beach at Khao Tao, scoring 8.4 from 123 reviews. Its charm is Sai Noi beach, which is quiet and very private, well away from the bustle of central Hua Hin about 12 km north. Rooms range from garden views with an outdoor shower to sea-view rooms and family bungalows, and there are pet-friendly rooms. Real guest reviews praise the quiet, the private beach and the restful feel. Worth knowing: it's far from town, so a car is more convenient.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Come for the quiet and the private beach — for waking to the sea, choose a Sea View Room. It's far from town, so bring a car and grab seafood at Khao Tao before checking in.

Small 12-room boutique with a restful feel
Sea-view rooms and pet-friendly rooms available
Balcony with outdoor shower in some rooms
cons: About 12 km from central Hua Hin — a car helps
8.4 score sits below the other resorts here; few restaurants nearby

entries.name: Takiab Beach Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Khao Takiap · Nong Kae · near Cicada Market, near the beach

rooms.type: Deluxe Room · front side, larger balcony
Family Room · near the kids' pool

entries.addr: 33/5-6 Khao Takiab, Nong Kae, Hua Hin, Prachuap Khiri Khan
entries.storyHtml: Takiab Beach Resort is a budget stay at Khao Takiap, from just ฿1,200 and close to the beach, scoring 8.1 from 39 reviews. It's a value pick for anyone who wants to be near Khao Takiap beach and Cicada Market without paying much. There's a pool, and rooms have AC, a fridge and a private balcony, plus family rooms. Real guest reviews praise the location near the beach and market, and the low price. Worth knowing: it's a budget property, with simple facilities and service rather than a luxury resort.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a larger front-facing balcony, choose the Deluxe Room. Walk to Cicada Market in the evening for good food — and set your expectations to a budget stay.
pros: From just ฿1,200, close to Khao Takiap beach
Near Cicada Market — walk over for evening food
Has a pool and family rooms
Rooms have AC, a fridge and a private balcony
cons: A budget property — simple facilities and service
Few reviews (39); 8.1 is the lowest score in the guide

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting rates for standard rooms and can change by date and season — always check live prices and compare 3 sites before booking. High season (November–February) brings cool, pleasant weather but more crowds and higher prices, especially on long weekends, New Year and Songkran, so book 1–2 months ahead, as Hua Hin is a top weekend escape for Bangkok residents. The rainy season (May–October) is cheaper and quieter. Hua Hin has no metro — getting around means your own car, rental car, scooter, and songthaews in town. Bangkok to Hua Hin is about 2.5–3 hours. faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Hua Hin hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in around Hua Hin?
faq.a: It depends on your travel style. Central Hua Hin beach is the hub — beach, malls, night market, train station, easiest to get around (Centara Grand, InterContinental, Asira, Maven, G Hua Hin, Litera). Khao Takiap has a wider, quieter beach at the southern end and is the beachfront resort zone (Hyatt Regency, Mövenpick, Anantasila, Takiab). Khao Tao / Sai Noi beach is a quiet, private beach about 12 km south of town (Sanae Beach).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Hua Hin hotels cost?
faq.a: There's a wide range: hostels and budget stays start around ฿390–1,800 a night; boutiques and 4-star run about ฿1,600–2,800; 5-star beachfront resorts start around ฿4,500–5,500+, with sea-view rooms and pool villas higher again. All prices are approximate starting rates for standard rooms; high season (Nov–Feb) and long weekends run well above normal.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Hua Hin hotel?
faq.a: On weekdays outside the tourist season, 2–4 weeks ahead is fine. But in high season (November–February), and especially on long weekends, New Year and Songkran, good rooms and beachfront resorts fill up fast — book 1–2 months ahead or more, since Hua Hin is a top weekend escape for Bangkok residents.

faq.q: ❓ How do I get to Hua Hin, and do I need a car?
faq.a: Bangkok to Hua Hin is about 2.5–3 hours by car, minivan or train. Within central Hua Hin there are songthaews and motorbike taxis, which work fine. But if you're staying at Khao Takiap or Khao Tao, having a car is much more convenient, as distances are longer and public transport is limited.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking Hua Hin hotels?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) vary by promotion at different times — we recommend opening all three and comparing before every booking. Each review page in this guide has price-comparison links, which can save you several hundred to over a thousand baht a night during peak periods.

faq.q: ❓ Is Hua Hin better for families or couples?
faq.a: It works for both. For families, choose somewhere with family rooms or pool villas, such as G Hua Hin (its own mall), Mövenpick Asara (all-suite pool villas) or Centara Grand. For couples and honeymooners, choose a beachfront boutique or design stay, such as Putahracsa (beachfront pool villas), Asira (rooms opening onto the pool) or Anantasila (quiet beachfront).
